properties.name: Lake Moeris (Faiyum), higher ancient level
properties.source: Faiyum lake-level history: Caton-Thompson & Gardner, The Desert Fayum (1934); Hassan (1986) on Holocene lake levels of the Faiyum. Modern Birket Qarun is at about -43 m; shorelines at +20 m are dated to the Middle Kingdom, the Early Dynastic level is uncertain, so +10 m is a hedge. The outline is hand-drawn around the depression.

properties.name: Head of the Persian Gulf, further inland (about 3000 BCE)
properties.source: Sea-level highstand c. 6000-4000 BP put the head of the Gulf far north-west of today's; Kennett & Kennett (2006), J. Island & Coastal Archaeology 1:67-99; Sanlaville & Dalongeville (2005); Pournelle (2003) on the marsh-delta landscape. Estimates of the line vary by tens of km; this is a deliberately conservative strip around the lower Shatt al-Arab.
